title: Associated Types
concept: Associated types let interfaces declare type placeholders that implementors fill in — like type Item for Iterator or type Output for function traits.
why: Without associated types, you'd need extra generic parameters cluttering every function. Associated types keep signatures clean and semantics clear.
tips: Use associated types when the type is naturally determined by the implementor
Use generic parameters when the caller should choose the type
Read Self::Item as 'the Item type associated with this implementation'
Associated types keep generic signatures clean — compare Iterator<Item=T> vs Iterator with type Item
common_mistakes: Using generic parameters where associated types would be clearer
Forgetting to specify the associated type in the impl block
Confusing associated type syntax: `type Item = T;` not `Item = T;`
